html:
The Bungandidj are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Mount Gambier region in the southeast of South Australia, and of nearby western Victoria. Their name was often written Boandik or Buandig. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their country is volcanic, with crater lakes such as the Blue Lake at Mount Gambier, limestone caves, wetlands and a long coastline. People caught fish and eels, and gathered roots and seafood. Settlers came in the 1840s, and the land was soon given over to sheep and later pine plantations. In 1880 Christina Smith, who had lived among them, published a book on their language and customs. Neighbours on the map include the Gunditjmara, the Bindjali and the Ngarrindjeri. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
